To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) older Australians with chronic medical conditions are at increased risk of not being able to afford out-of- pocket health care expenses and 2) this risk is increased with the number and severity of chronic medical conditions.

1) almost 4% of Australians aged 50 and older were unable to afford at least one out-of-pocket health expense in the previous 12 months; and 2) older Australians with three or more long-term chronic health conditions are more likely to report being unable to afford medical costs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact that chronic conditions and multimorbidity have on the affordability of health care for older Australians.
the affordability of out-of-pocket expenses for medical and allied health services among older Australians.
the financial impact of health care on older Australians and the implications of this for the health care system and the economy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Australian health care system is not equitable, affordable and sustainable.
the study found that 4% of older Australians are unable to afford out of pocket medical expenses and this is more common in those with multiple chronic conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
older people with chronic conditions face a financial burden from out of pocket health care expenses, even with Australia's universal health care system.
the cost of health care in Australia is a significant burden on older Australians, especially those with multiple chronic health problems.
older Australians are at high risk for not being able to afford their health care expenses.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Australian health system is not equitable, as older Australians with chronic conditions are at increased risk of being unable pay for out-of-pocket costs for medical and pharmaceutical care, dental care, allied health care and transport to medical and dental appointments.

the current health care safety nets are inadequate for the growing number of older Australians with multiple long-term medical conditions, and the financial burden of out-of-pocket medical expenses should be addressed.
the out-of-pocket costs associated with health care in Australia are a significant financial burden to many older Australians, especially those with multimorbidity.
